edition.name: Migne, Patrologia Latina (PL 2, Paris 1844), De praescriptionibus adversus haereticos, via Latin Wikisource transcription
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Si haec ita se habent, ut veritas nobis adjudicetur, quicumque in ea regula incedimus quam Ecclesia ab Apostolis, Apostoli a Christo, Christus a Deo tradidit, constat ratio propositi nostri, definientis non esse admittendos haereticos ad ineundam de Scripturis provocationem, quos sine Scripturis probamus ad Scripturas non pertinere. Si enim haeretici sunt, christiani esse non possunt, non a Christo habendo quod de sua electione sectati haereticorum nomine admittunt. Ita non christiani, nullum jus capiunt christianarum litterarum. Ad quos merito dicendum est: Qui estis? quando, et unde venistis? quid in meo agitis, non mei? quo denique, Marcion, jure sylvam meam caedis? qua licentia, Valentine, fontes meos transvertis? qua potestate, Apelles, limites meos commoves? Quid hic caeteri ad voluntatem vestram seminatis et pascitis? Mea est possessio; olim possideo: habeo origines firmas, ab ipsis auctoribus quorum fuit res. Ego sum haeres Apostolorum. Sicut caverunt testamento suo, sicut fidei commiserunt, sicut adjuraverunt, ita teneo. Vos certe exhaeredaverunt semper et abdicaverunt, ut extraneos, ut inimicos. Unde autem extranei et inimici Apostolis haeretici, nisi ex diversitate doctrinae, quam unusquisque de suo arbitrio adversus Apostolos, aut protulit, aut recepit?
pass_a_gloss: If these things are thus, that truth is adjudged to us, whoever we are who walk in that rule which the Church handed down from the Apostles, the Apostles from Christ, Christ from God, it is established the reason of our proposal, defining that heretics are not to be admitted to undertaking a challenge from the Scriptures, whom we prove without the Scriptures not to pertain to the Scriptures. For if they are heretics, they cannot be Christians, not having from Christ what they admit by the name of heretics, having followed their own election. Thus not being Christians, they take no right of Christian writings. To whom it is to be said with merit: Who are you? when, and from where have you come? what are you doing in my thing, not mine? by what right, finally, Marcion, do you cut down my forest? with what license, Valentine, do you divert my springs? with what power, Apelles, do you move my boundaries? What are the rest of you sowing and feeding here according to your will? Mine is the possession; I have long been in possession: I have firm origins, from the very authors to whom the thing belonged. I am the heir of the Apostles. Just as they took precautions by their testament, just as they entrusted to faith, just as they adjured, so I hold. You, certainly, have always been disinherited and renounced, as strangers, as enemies. But from where are heretics strangers and enemies to the Apostles, if not from the diversity of doctrine, which each one either produced or received from his own judgment against the Apostles?
pass_b_english: If things stand this way—if the truth is awarded to us, who follow the rule that the Church received from the Apostles, the Apostles from Christ, Christ from God—then the logic of our position is settled: heretics must not be admitted to a contest over Scripture, because we prove, even without Scripture, that they have no claim on it. If they are heretics, they cannot be Christians; they possess nothing from Christ, having chosen to follow their own preference and taken the name 'heretic.' Not being Christians, they hold no right to Christian writings. We are therefore justified in demanding: Who are you? When and where did you come from? What are you doing on my property—property that is not yours? By what right, Marcion, do you cut down my forest? By what license, Valentine, do you divert my springs? By what authority, Apelles, do you move my boundary markers? What are the rest of you sowing and grazing here at your own pleasure? This possession is mine; I have held it for a long time. My title is firm, traced back to the very authors to whom the truth belonged. I am the heir of the Apostles. Just as they safeguarded it in their testament, entrusted it to the faith, and bound it with an oath, so I hold it. You, on the other hand, have always been disinherited and renounced—strangers, enemies. And how else could heretics be strangers and enemies to the Apostles except through a divergence in doctrine, which each one either invented or adopted on his own authority against the Apostles?

review.notes: All clauses in the Latin source were checked against Pass A and Pass B. Pass A preserves the literal structure and nuances (e.g., 'adjudicetur' as 'is adjudged', 'exhaeredaverunt' as 'have been disinherited'). Pass B provides a fluent rendering that maintains the meaning and agency of the original. No omissions or contradictions were found.
